p.src: Now Song Jiang returned home in glory, then went back to the Eastern Capital and rejoined his brothers, ordering each man to pack his belongings and proceed to his appointed post. Presently Dai Zong, the “Magic Traveler,” came to visit Song Jiang, and the two sat talking at leisure. Suddenly Dai Zong rose and said, “By His Majesty’s grace, I have been appointed commander-in-chief of Yanzhou. Yet I now wish to surrender my patent of office, go to the Temple of the Sacred Peak in Tai’an Prefecture, and serve there as a resident attendant. If I can spend the rest of my life in that place, I shall count myself truly fortunate.” Song Jiang said, “Brother, what has put such a thought into your mind?” Dai Zong replied, “Last night I dreamed that Judge Cui summoned me, and that awakened this pious resolve.” Song Jiang said, “Brother, since in this life you have been the ‘Magic Traveler,’ one day you will surely become an all-knowing spirit in the court of the Sacred Peak.” After they parted, Dai Zong surrendered his patent of office and went to the Temple of the Sacred Peak in Tai’an Prefecture. There he took religious vows as a resident attendant and every day diligently tended the incense offerings to the Holy Emperor, never once failing in devotion. Several months later, one evening while in perfect health, he summoned his fellow Daoists, bade each of them farewell, and died with a great laugh. Thereafter he repeatedly manifested his divine power in the temple. The people and temple custodians of the prefecture accordingly fashioned an image of the deified Dai Zong there, with his preserved mortal remains enshrined within it. Ruan Xiaoqi, too, received his imperial patent, took leave of Song Jiang, and went to serve as commander-in-chief of the Gaitian Army. Before many months had passed, the generals Wang Bing and Zhao Tan, still nursing resentment over the insults they had suffered at Bangyuan Cave, repeatedly denounced Ruan Xiaoqi’s offenses before Privy Councillor Tong. They said that he had once put on Fang La’s russet-yellow imperial robe, dragon gown, and jade belt; though done in a moment of sport, it showed that he had long harbored evil intentions. Moreover, they claimed, the Gaitian Army was stationed in a remote and savage region, so he would inevitably rebel. Tong Guan reported the matter to Cai Jing, who memorialized the emperor and obtained an imperial decree. Official documents were sent there ordering that Ruan Xiaoqi’s patent and rank be revoked and that he be reduced once more to a commoner. When Ruan Xiaoqi learned of it, he was inwardly delighted. Taking his aged mother with him, he returned to Shijie Village in the Liangshan Marsh and once more made his living by fishing. He supported his mother and lived out his allotted years, dying later at the age of sixty.

p.src: Now Chai Jin, the “Little Whirlwind,” was in the capital and saw that Dai Zong had surrendered his patent of office and retired. He also heard that the court had revoked Ruan Xiaoqi’s patent and reduced him to a commoner because he had improperly worn Fang La’s Heaven-Leveling Crown, dragon robe, and jade belt, allegedly intending to imitate Fang La’s rebellion. He thought, “I too once served as Fang La’s imperial son-in-law. If the treacherous ministers should learn of it someday and slander me before the emperor, bringing charges against me and stripping me of my patent, would I not suffer humiliation?” “Better to recognize the times myself and escape such disgrace.” He therefore claimed that recurrent attacks of palsy made him unfit for office and voluntarily surrendered his patent, asking leave to retire and become a farmer. Taking leave of the officials, he returned to Henghai Commandery in Cangzhou, lived as a commoner, and passed his days in freedom. Then one day he suddenly died without illness. Li Ying was appointed commander-in-chief of Zhongshan Prefecture. After serving there for half a year, he heard that Chai Jin had retired. He too reflected upon his position and claimed to be paralyzed by palsy and unable to remain in office. He petitioned the provincial authorities, surrendered his patent, and returned to his native village at Dulong Ridge to live. Thereafter he and Du Xing became wealthy landowners together, and both died peaceful deaths. Guan Sheng commanded the troops at Daming Prefecture in Beijing. He won the hearts of his soldiers, and all admired and obeyed him. One day, returning from drilling his troops, he became very drunk, lost his footing, and fell from his horse. He took ill from the fall and died. Huyan Zhuo was appointed commander of the Imperial Camp and attended the emperor each day in military readiness. Later he led a great army against Wuzhu, the Fourth Prince of the Jin, and defeated him. Advancing with his troops as far as western Huai, he fell in battle. Only Zhu Tong earned distinction commanding troops in Baoding Prefecture. Later he followed Liu Guangshi in defeating the Jin and eventually rose to become military governor of the Taiping Army. Hua Rong took his wife, children, and younger sister with him and went to assume his post in Yingtian Prefecture. Wu Yong had always been unmarried, so he took only a young attendant and went to assume his post with the Wusheng Army. Li Kui likewise traveled alone with two servants to take up his post in Runzhou. But why have we spoken only of these three assuming their posts, while already relating the final fates of all the others? It is because those seven principal commanders were never to meet one another again, and so their endings have been told first. The remaining five principal commanders—Song Jiang, Lu Junyi, Hua Rong, Wu Yong, and Li Kui—would meet again. Their stories have therefore not yet been brought to a close; their final fates will presently be revealed.

p.src: To return to Song Jiang and Lu Junyi: while still in the capital, they distributed the rewards among all the commanders and ordered each man to proceed to his appointed post. As for those who had died in imperial service, their dependent families and household members were issued gracious awards of money, silk, gold, and silver, then sent back to their native places to live as they pleased. Of the fifteen surviving secondary commanders then present at court, Song Jiang’s brother Song Qing returned home to farm, while Du Xing had already followed Li Ying back to their native place. Huang Xin remained in his post at Qingzhou. Sun Li took his brother Sun Xin, Gu Dasao, and his own wife and children with him and continued in his former service at Dengzhou. Zou Run had no wish to become an official and returned to Mount Dengyun. Cai Qing followed Guan Sheng back to Beijing and lived there as a commoner. After consulting with Yang Lin, Pei Xuan returned to Yinmachuan, accepted an appointment, and then sought retirement. Jiang Jing longed for his native place and chose to return to Tanzhou as a commoner. Zhu Wu went to learn Daoist arts from Fan Rui. The two became Quanzhen masters and wandered throughout the land, then joined Gongsun Sheng and entered the religious life, living out their natural years. Mu Chun returned to his native Jieyang Town and once more became an honest commoner. Ling Zhen’s skill with cannon was extraordinary, so he remained in imperial service at the Gunpowder Bureau. Of the five secondary commanders who had previously remained in the capital, An Daoquan had been summoned back by imperial command and made a Gold-and-Purple Medical Officer in the Imperial Medical Academy. Huangfu Duan had originally been appointed chief commissioner of the Imperial Stables. Jin Dajian was already serving as an official in the Imperial Seal Office within the palace. Xiao Rang received a post in Grand Preceptor Cai’s residence and served as a learned household secretary. Yue He spent his old age in ease in the residence of Prince Consort Commandant Wang, enjoying happiness for the rest of his life. Of them, there is no more to tell.

Even under the present Son of Heaven, Emperor Huizong, a sovereign of supreme wisdom and discernment, it so happened that wicked ministers controlled the court, slanderous flatterers monopolized power, and loyal and worthy men suffered injustice—a deeply lamentable state of affairs. At that time the four villainous ministers Cai Jing, Tong Guan, Gao Qiu, and Yang Jian threw the realm into disorder, ruining the state, its families, and its people. Gao Qiu, grand commandant of the Palace Command, and Yang Jian saw the Son of Heaven honor Song Jiang and his fellow officers with rich gifts, and they were deeply displeased. The two met privately and said, “Song Jiang and Lu Junyi are both our enemies, yet today they have become ministers of merit and received such favor from the court, with authority over the army on horseback and the people when dismounted. How can officials of the central ministries like us escape the ridicule of others? As the old saying goes, ‘He who will not avenge the slightest grudge is no gentleman; he who is not ruthless is no true man!’” Yang Jian said, “I have a plan. If we dispose of Lu Junyi first, we shall cut off one of Song Jiang’s arms. He is exceedingly valiant. p.src: Once the two villainous ministers had settled their scheme, they sent trusted agents to find two natives of Luzhou, wrote out a complaint for them, and ordered them to accuse Pacification Commissioner Lu before the Bureau of Military Affairs, alleging that he was presently recruiting soldiers, buying horses, gathering fodder, and stockpiling grain in Luzhou with the intention of rebelling; and that he frequently sent men to Chuzhou to conspire with Pacification Commissioner Song Jiang and coordinate an uprising. The Bureau of Military Affairs was headed by Tong Guan, who likewise bore a grudge against Song Jiang and the others. He immediately accepted the plaintiffs’ complaint and sent it directly to the Grand Preceptor’s residence for presentation to the throne. When Cai Jing saw the memorial, he summoned the officials to deliberate. Gao Qiu and Yang Jian were both present. The four treacherous ministers settled their plan and led the plaintiffs into the palace to report the matter to the Son of Heaven. His Majesty said, “As I recall, Song Jiang and Lu Junyi campaigned against foes in every quarter and held command over a hundred thousand troops, yet even then they entertained no evil intent. Now that they have abandoned evil and returned to righteousness, how could they consent to revolt? I have never treated them unjustly; how would they dare rebel against the court? …There may be deceit in this. Until we know whether the charge is false or true, it cannot readily be believed.” Gao Qiu and Yang Jian, who stood nearby, memorialized, “Though Your Majesty’s reasoning is sound, the human heart is difficult to fathom. Lu Junyi must be dissatisfied with the low rank and humble office he received. He conceived thoughts of rebellion once more and unfortunately was discovered.” His Majesty said, “Summon him here. I shall question him personally and make him confess the truth.” Cai Jing and Tong Guan further memorialized, “Lu Junyi is a ferocious beast whose intentions cannot be trusted. If he is alarmed, he will surely escape. That would be most inconvenient, and it would be difficult to capture him afterward. We should merely lure him to the capital. Your Majesty can personally bestow imperial food and wine upon him, soothe him with gracious words, and observe whether the accusation is true and how he behaves. If he is innocent, there will be no need to investigate further, and Your Majesty’s solicitude in not betraying a meritorious minister will also be made manifest.” His Majesty approved their proposal and immediately issued an edict, dispatching an envoy directly to Luzhou to summon Lu Junyi back to court on the pretext that he was to be given an appointment. The imperial envoy obeyed his orders and reached Luzhou. Officials great and small went beyond the city walls to welcome him and escorted him straight to the prefectural offices, where the edict was read aloud. There is no need to belabor the account. On hearing the edict summoning him back to court, Lu Junyi left Luzhou with the envoy, and together they mounted post horses and set out for the capital. Nothing of note happened on the road, and before long they reached the Imperial City Office in the Eastern Capital, where they lodged. Early the next day, Lu went outside Donghua Gate to await the morning audience. Grand Preceptor Cai Jing, Military Affairs Commissioner Tong Guan, and Grand Commandants Gao Qiu and Yang Jian then led Lu Junyi into a side hall for an audience with His Majesty. After Lu had completed his prostrations, the Son of Heaven said, “I wished to see you.” He then asked, “Can you make a satisfactory life for yourself in Luzhou?” Lu Junyi bowed twice and replied, “By the boundless blessing of Your Majesty, the soldiers and people there all live in peace and security.” His Majesty asked a few more casual questions. When the audience had dragged on until noon, an official of the Imperial Kitchen reported, “The imperial meal has been presented, but we dare not serve it on our own authority. We beg Your Majesty’s command.” By then Gao Qiu and Yang Jian had secretly put mercury into the food, which was presented on the imperial table. In his presence, the Son of Heaven bestowed the meal upon Lu Junyi. Lu Junyi bowed, accepted it, and ate. His Majesty gently admonished him, “When you return to Luzhou, you must apply yourself wholeheartedly, care well for the soldiers, and entertain no improper designs.” Lu Junyi knocked his head upon the floor and thanked the emperor for his grace. He left the court and returned to Luzhou, wholly unaware that the four villainous ministers had plotted to kill him. Gao Qiu and Yang Jian said to each other, “Now the great affair is settled!”

Though the place was small, peaks encircled it; its contours crouched like dragon and tiger, with winding ridges, slopes, terraces, and stonework. Creeks branched all around it, with lakes and marshes before and behind, exactly like the stronghold among the waters of Liangshan Marsh. Song Jiang was delighted by the sight and thought, “If I were to die here, it would make a fitting resting place.” Whenever he was free, he went there to roam, delighting his heart and passing the time. Song Jiang said, “Brother, since we parted, I have thought of all our comrades day and night. Strategist Wu Yong is far away with the Wusheng Army, and Stockade Commander Hua is in Yingtian Prefecture; I do not even know how they fare. Only you, brother, are nearby at Zhenjiang in Runzhou, so I have specially asked you here to discuss a matter of great importance.” Li Kui asked, “Elder brother, what great matter is it?” Song Jiang said, “Have some wine first!” Song Jiang invited him into the rear hall, where cups and dishes already stood ready, and at once entertained Li Kui with food and wine for a long while. When they were nearly half drunk, Song Jiang said, “Good brother, you do not know that I have heard the court sent a man bearing poisoned wine and bestowed it on me to drink. If I die, what are we to do?” Li Kui cried out, “Elder brother, then let us rebel!” Song Jiang said, “Brother, all our forces are gone, and our comrades have scattered in every direction. How could a rebellion succeed?” Li Kui said, “I have three thousand troops at Zhenjiang. Muster all your Chuzhou troops too, and rouse every one of these common people. Then we can pool our strength, recruit soldiers, buy horses, and fight our way forward! It would be far happier simply to return to Liangshan Marsh! Anything is better than suffering humiliation under those treacherous ministers!” Song Jiang said, “Wait, brother. We shall consider it further.” In fact, a slow-acting poison had already been placed in the welcome wine. Li Kui drank that night, and the next day a boat was prepared to see him off. As he lay dying, Li Kui instructed his attendants, “After I die, you must take my coffin to Liaor Marsh outside the southern gate of Chuzhou and bury me beside my elder brother.” Having given these instructions, he died. Greatly startled, the Retired Emperor repeatedly asked, “Who are all of you?” The leader, wearing a golden helmet with phoenix-wing ornaments, a brocade robe, and golden armor, stepped forward and reported, “Your servant is Song Jiang of Liangshan Marsh.” The Retired Emperor said, “I appointed you Pacification Commissioner in Chuzhou. Why are you here?” Song Jiang replied, “We humbly beg Your Majesty to come into the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness, so that I may relate in full our true feelings and the injustice of our wrongful deaths.” The Retired Emperor dismounted before the Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness and took his seat inside. Looking below the hall, he saw many people prostrate amid the mist. The Retired Emperor remained hesitant and uncertain. Then Song Jiang, who stood at their head, ascended the steps, came forward on his knees, and made his appeal through falling tears. The Retired Emperor asked, “Why do you weep?” Song Jiang replied, “Though we once resisted the imperial army, we always held fast to loyalty and righteousness and never harbored the slightest disloyal intent. Since accepting amnesty by Your Majesty’s decree, we first drove back the Liao army and then subdued three bands of rebels; eight out of every ten of our brothers were lost. By Your Majesty’s command I guarded Chuzhou, and from the day I took office I accepted not so much as water or rice from soldiers or commoners; Heaven and Earth bear witness. Now Your Majesty has bestowed medicinal wine upon me and had me drink it; I die without regret. But I feared that Li Kui might nurse resentment and recklessly conceive rebellious designs; so I deliberately sent someone to Runzhou to summon Li Kui, and personally gave him poisoned wine, killing him with it. Wu Yong and Hua Rong also came out of loyalty and righteousness and hanged themselves at my grave. The four of us were buried together at Liao’er Hollow outside the south gate of Chuzhou. The local people took pity on us and built a shrine before our graves. Now our spirits have not dispersed but have all gathered here to appeal to Your Majesty and declare the true sentiments we held throughout our lives, unchanged from beginning to end. We beg Your Majesty to judge us with divine discernment.” Greatly shocked by what he heard, the Retired Emperor said, “I personally selected an imperial envoy and had him bestow sealed imperial wine upon you. I do not know who exchanged it for poisoned wine and gave it to you.” Song Jiang replied, “Your Majesty need only question the envoy who came, and the source of the treachery will become known.” Seeing how imposing the three passes and stockades were, the Retired Emperor asked mournfully, “What place is this, where you have all assembled?” Song Jiang replied, “This is Liangshan Marsh, where we once gathered in brotherhood.” The Retired Emperor said again, “You are already dead and ought to go on to rebirth. Why have you gathered here?” Song Jiang replied, “The Great Emperor took pity on our loyalty and righteousness, and by a writ and decree from the Jade Emperor we were enfeoffed as the collective tutelary gods of Liangshan Marsh. All the generals have gathered here, for we suffered an injustice we could not redress. We therefore sent Dai Zong to trouble the sovereign of the realm to come in person to the marsh, so that we might earnestly declare the true feelings we have always held.” The Retired Emperor said, “Why did you not come to the innermost imperial palace and manifest yourselves before me there?” Song Jiang replied, “I am but a spirit dwelling in the dark realm. How could I reach the phoenix gates and dragon towers of the palace? Now that Your Majesty has left the palace precincts, we have presumed to invite you here.” The Retired Emperor asked, “May I look around?” Song Jiang and the others bowed twice in gratitude for the favor. The Retired Emperor descended from the hall and looked back at the plaque above it. On it were written in large characters the three words “Hall of Loyalty and Righteousness.” He nodded and went down the steps. Suddenly Li Kui came around from behind Song Jiang, gripping a pair of axes, and shouted fiercely, “Emperor! Emperor! How could you listen to the slanders of those four treacherous ministers and wrongfully cost us our lives? Now that I have met you today, this is the perfect chance to take revenge!” No sooner had the Black Whirlwind spoken than he swung up both axes and charged straight at the Retired Emperor.

p.src: Do not blame Heaven for the course of rise and retreat; the extermination of Han Xin’s and Peng Yue’s clans was pity enough. With one heart they served the realm on days they broke the foe; through a hundred battles they captured Liao and crushed Fang La. The baleful luminaries and Heavenly Stars are gone now, yet slanderous ministers and treacherous villains remain as before! Had they known the poison would bury them beneath the yellow earth, they might have followed Fan Li of Chiyi and taken to his boat.

u.src: And another poem:

p.src: In life they dined from the cauldrons of the great; in death they were enfeoffed as marquises—the ambitions of their manhood were fulfilled. Iron steeds neigh at night as the moon over the hills gives way to dawn; dark gibbons cry in autumn beneath thickening evening clouds. No need to seek the true traces of their advance and retreat; rejoice instead that loyal and worthy men have become the subject of this tale. For a thousand ages, Liao’er Marsh shall be the ground where jade lies buried; falling blossoms and crying birds alike awaken sorrow.
